text:
sarah_support: Hey team — customer Velociti on dedicated cluster eu-west-1-ded-42 is seeing sustained TPS SLO violations this morning. They report lots of 429s and elevated p95 latency. Burst credits show 0. Can someone triage?
ian_oncall: Thanks Sarah. When did this start and do they have a reproducible test? Any recent deploys?
sarah_support: Started ~07:12UTC. No deploys reported. Customer says spike came from a marketing campaign + a cron job running at the same time. They shared this snippet of client errors:```json
{"time":"2026-03-17T07:12:25Z","status":429,"error":"admission_rejected","reason":"burst_credits_exhausted"}```
leena_cust_eng: Added their traffic pattern: lots of short requests (avg tokens 12) at high concurrency, many parallel connections from mobile clients. They also do occasional batch inference. This seems to be a noisy-tenant profile vs steady streaming.
mike_infra: I pulled the cluster metrics. Autoscaler didn't add nodes because admission headroom threshold is 0.15 and the pool reported 18% free GPU capacity but admission tokens were already depleted by prefix-burst accounting. Looks like burst credits were consumed by many small requests that bypassed queueing.
ian_oncall: Can you paste the admission controller logs? Also what does /internal/v1/admission/status show?
mike_infra: Pasting relevant lines:```
[07:11:58] admit-controller: admit check account=velociti credits_remaining=0 req_tps=85 limit_tps=50 -> REJECT
[07:12:01] kvcache: high contention for model=redwood-medium seq=16
[07:12:03] autoscaler: scale_decision=no_scale reason=policy_headroom_satisfied free_gpu=0.18````
admitbot: SYSTEM: account velociti burst_credits=0, last_refill=2026-03-16T00:00:00Z, burst_window=24h. Consider refill or reserved capacity.
jordan_prod: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) enable model-fallback to redwood-small for this customer (cheaper token cost & lower KV pressure), 2) increase temporary burst allocation for the account, 3) route their traffic to a regional spare pool if available. Long-term: tune admission accounting to weight short requests less aggressively and add prefix aggregation to reduce credit burn.
sarah_support: Customer asked for repro steps so they can test after we change config. Suggested repro: run a short stress with many concurrent clients doing 12-token requests at 100 TPS for 10m. Provide them a curl example?
ian_oncall: Send them this quick repro script (they can run from k6 or a small loop):```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait```
leena_cust_eng: Also asked me to confirm whether admission logs would show whether rejections are due to burst vs sustained limit. Admission does differentiate (we log reason). We'll share logs after we apply mitigation.
mike_infra: Immediate steps I'm taking: 1) temporarily grant +30s burst credits to velociti, 2) enable fallback to redwood-small on their route, 3) open a canary route to eu-west-1-spare-pool. Rolling now — ETA 5m.
admitbot: ACTION: granted 30s burst_credit to account velociti by mike_infra (trace=tr-2101-ctl).
ops_bot: Reminder created: ticket #SUP-2101 assigned to mike_infra; follow-up in 4h for capacity plan.
sarah_support: Noted. I'll message the customer that we're applying temporary credits and a fallback, and ask them to run the repro.
jordan_prod: Post-mortem ask: add a headroom-safety check to autoscaler to prefer scale-out when admission rejections > 5% for 1m. Also add a short-request weighting tweak. I'll create a story.
ian_oncall: After Mike's changes, monitor p95 and rejection rate. If we still see >1% 429s we'll escalate to capacity ops.
mike_infra: Updated: canary route enabled, fallback active. Early signals show rejected rate down from 12% -> 1.6%. KV cache contention dropping. Will keep watching. :thumbsup:
sarah_support: Customer confirmed they can complete repro without 429s now. They still want guidance on headroom planning for marketing spikes.
leena_cust_eng: Action items for cust eng: 1) share best-practice doc for bursty traffic (stagger cron, client-side backoff), 2) recommend reserved capacity commit if they expect repeated high spikes.
ops_bot: Follow-up scheduled: run a 72h audit of burst credit consumption for velociti and similar profiles (owner: jordan_prod).
jordan_prod: I'll draft the headroom playbook and propose an admission policy change. Assigning myself.
sarah_support: Thanks all — please keep thread updated if anything regresses.
ian_oncall: Closing loop for now, will reopen if we get new rejections.
